# /crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs

lane: cross-cutting | group: Keep the picture current | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.124.0 | prompts: 4
purpose: Sweep linked repos for changed branches and open or recently closed pull requests, and feed them into the specs.
use_when: Many repos or pull requests should be caught up into the specs
prompt_note: The flow question only when the word is absent, the manual start batch (fetch and, when a specs-repo row exists, its pull request comments), the inventory confirm, and the current item or small group. Auto-flow asks nothing once the word is present. A number of minutes the user left out uses 20 and is outside the budget. Each later item is a later turn.
reads: Reads `docs/system/repos.md`, `Synced at` lines, the sweep progress file, sibling checkouts, and pull request threads through the same `gh` or `az` reads add-to-spec already uses. It does not read Slack, mail, issues, or production data. It does not log in.
writes: Writes `docs/system/sweep-progress.md` through `scripts/sweep_progress.py --vendor copilot`. Runs `/crav1-add-to-spec` so that skill can write the PR note, its record, and `Synced at`. Writes one `Read: sweep` line on a PR note whose threads were read. Manual flow writes a spec line only after the change is shown and the user says yes. Auto flow does not write spec lines; it records proposals in the progress file.
leaves alone: Leaves base branches, the specs repo's branches, a person's `Read` line, and every thread on the host alone. Does not run `/crav1-review-pr` or `/crav1-pr-status`. Does not commit, push, or delete.
limits: No flow word asks, and a headless run with no word stops. Auto flow cannot record a spec write. A fetch failure skips that repo. The first sweep has no closed-since list. A budget stop finishes the current item and resumes later.
flow:
- `/crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs` is one skill with `manual-flow` and `auto-flow`.
- It runs `/crav1-add-to-spec` for each changed branch and each open or recently closed pull request, including drafts and the host conversation and review threads.
- An optional repo name narrows the run to one `docs/system/repos.md` row.
- Default scope is every row with a URL that is not `proposed`, except the specs repo.
- Base branches (`main`, `master`, `develop`, `release/*`, and `Merges into`) are not items.
- Slack, mail, issues, and a new `/crav1-review-pr` are out.
- Auto flow fetches without asking and writes notes and `Synced at` only.
- State is `docs/system/sweep-progress.md`, written only by `scripts/sweep_progress.py --vendor copilot`.
- A pull request whose threads were read gets one `Read: sweep` line on its PR note.
- The budget is 20 minutes unless a number is given, and the script will not go past 45.
- The run does not commit, push, post, vote, resolve a thread, or run `/crav1-review-pr`, `/crav1-pr-status`, `/crav1-resolve-open-questions`, or `/crav1-finalize-commit`.
- Next is this command when items or proposals remain, or `/crav1-resolve-open-questions` when a conflict or open question was written onto a spec.
- each item opens `../crav1-add-to-spec/SKILL.md` and follows that item's choice words.
- It does not start `/crav1-add-to-spec` as a command.
- The rule is `docs/reference/open-skill-file.md`.

## Choice words
- question: Which flow
  - `manual-flow`: Ask once before fetching, confirm the inventory, then show each spec change before writing it. An optional repo may follow.
  - `auto-flow`: Fetch without asking. Write notes and Synced at only. Spec changes stay proposals. An optional repo may follow.
  note: The repo is an optional repos.md name, not the characters [repo]. A whole number of minutes may follow. The specs repo stays out unless it is named, or manual-flow is told to read its pull request comments. Its branches are never read.
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Opens `/crav1-add-to-spec` for each inventory item and follows that skill's note and `Synced at` rules. It does not start that command. It does not run `/crav1-review-pr`, `/crav1-pr-status`, `/crav1-resolve-open-questions`, or `/crav1-finalize-commit`.
you run next: /crav1-resolve-open-questions; /crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs; /crav1-finalize-commit
first: `/crav1-update-specs-from-changes-and-prs manual-flow <optional repo, or leave it out>`
